reading.body:
Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico has received $2.5 billion in investment since its 2016 groundbreaking and operates with 400 dedicated staff once complete. The specific IT capacity in megawatts is not published by Meta, and no published power figure exists for any facility in New Mexico, so the scale of this campus relative to others in the state cannot be determined from operator disclosures. A Meta-supported renewable energy project is adding 885 megawatts of generation and 100 megawatts of battery storage to the state grid, indicating material commitment to the power infrastructure that constrains AI scaling in the region.

The campus operates under LEED Gold certification and Meta reports matching all electricity use with 100 percent clean and renewable energy as part of global net-zero operations. The absence of a published megawatt figure prevents comparison to other hyperscale sites and means the campus's current and future grid demand must be inferred from industry norms rather than operator specification. New Mexico has 14 mapped data center facilities but zero published power capacity across all operators, making this campus characteristic of the disclosure gap that limits visibility into regional AI infrastructure buildout.

Meta's local employment commitment, educational funding, and water positivity pledge signal a multi-decade operational posture at this site. The lack of published specifications is not unique to this campus in the state, but it means the actual binding constraint this facility places on New Mexico's grid remains opaque to external analysis.
